# Before anything is taken from the branch being merged in, that branch is
# checked out into the tmp dir and verified as a whole - the same check `sesam
# verify` runs. Its state is left behind so the driver runs that follow (git
# calls one per conflicting path) reuse it instead of repeating the work.

sesam-repo admin base.txt mine.txt theirs.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt a
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt b
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt c
exec sesam add a --group admin
exec sesam add b --group admin
exec sesam add c --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add a b c'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt a
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt b
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt c
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change all three'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt a
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt b
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt c
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: change all three'

# All three conflict, so the driver runs three times.
! exec git merge topic
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file a'
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file b'
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file c'

# One state file covers all three, and the branch it came from is unpacked
# beside it rather than checked out over the worktree.
exec ls .sesam/tmp
stdout 'theirs-vstate\.json'
stdout '^theirs$'

# It really is the incoming branch's state: it knows the secrets, and it is
# readable as plain json.
grep '"RevealedPath":"a"' .sesam/tmp/theirs-vstate.json
grep '"name":"admin"' .sesam/tmp/theirs-vstate.json

# Finishing the merge still works and leaves a repo that verifies.
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt a
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt b
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt c
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

# The scratch space is emptied by the finalize - the unpacked branch is a full
# copy of their .sesam and would otherwise pile up, one per merge.
exec ls .sesam/tmp
! stdout 'theirs'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- mine.txt --
MINE
-- theirs.txt --
THEIRS
